ru-KZ.notes: Neither store has a Kazakhstan-specific Russian; use generic ru / ru-RU. The App Store KAZ storefront can show the ru listing.

kk-KZ.notes: iOS offers Kazakh as a system language, so a kk.lproj UI will show, but App Store Connect has no Kazakh listing locale (use the ru listing for the KAZ storefront).

uz-UZ.lproj: uz-Latn (or uz; CLDR default script for uz is Latn) - unverified against Apple docs
uz-UZ.notes: Not a store listing language on either store, and not an iOS system language (keyboard only). An uz lproj would not be selected: per-app language only lists system languages. Badge per third-party mirror of Google's badge set only.

az-AZ.notes: Apple badge exists ('Azərbaycan dili') even though there is no App Store listing or iOS system language. An iOS az lproj would not be shown.

ka-GE.notes: Play only. An iOS ka lproj would not be shown.

hy-AM.notes: Play only. An iOS hy lproj would not be shown.

sq-AL.notes: Play only. An iOS sq lproj would not be shown.

mk-MK.notes: Play only. An iOS mk lproj would not be shown.

bs-BA.lproj: bs (Latin is the CLDR default; bs-Latn if explicit) - unverified against Apple docs
bs-BA.notes: Neither store has a Bosnian listing (Play only has hr and sr). Not an iOS system language or keyboard. Badge per third-party mirror only.

bn-BD.notes: Apple's help page calls it 'Bangla'; the ASC API table calls it 'Bengali' (bn-BD). It is one of the 11 languages ASC added in March 2026; one third-party report says the bare code 'bn' is rejected by the API.

ne-NP.notes: Play only. An iOS ne lproj would not be shown.

si-LK.notes: Play only. An iOS si lproj would not be shown.

ta-LK.notes: Both stores only offer India Tamil (ta-IN); there is no ta-LK. Listings would be authored under ta-IN. Apple added Tamil in March 2026. Use the plain ta.lproj on iOS.

km-KH.notes: Play only. An iOS km lproj would not be shown.

lo-LA.notes: Play only. An iOS lo lproj would not be shown.

mn-MN.notes: Play only. An iOS mn lproj would not be shown.

fil-PH.notes: Play only. Apple's badge list has 'Tagalog' but not 'Filipino', and that badge is probably usable. An iOS fil lproj would not be shown.

sw-TZ.notes: Play only. An iOS sw lproj would not be shown.

am-ET.notes: Play listing is supported, but 'am' is not in the 76-code mirror of Google's badge set, and Google's official badge folder could not be listed without signing in. An iOS am lproj would not be shown.

sources: https://developer.apple.com/help/app-store-connect/reference/app-store-localizations — 50 listing languages by name; includes Bangla, Catalan, Hindi, Russian, Tamil, Ukrainian, Urdu; none of the other 16 asked about

https://developer.apple.com/documentation/appstoreconnectapi/managing-metadata-in-your-app-by-using-locale-shortcodes — ASC API locale codes: uk, ru, ca, hi, bn-BD (Bengali), ur-PK, ta-IN, plus the rest of the 50
https://9to5mac.com/2026/03/31/app-store-connect-adds-11-new-languages-for-localized-app-metadata/ — Mar 2026: 11 languages added (incl. Bangla, Tamil, Urdu), total 50
https://support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/9844778 — Play listing languages and codes; Uzbek and Bosnian absent; Tamil only ta-IN; Russian ru-RU; Kazakh kk

https://www.apple.com/ios/feature-availability/ (System Language section, iOS/iPadOS 26) — includes Bangla, Catalan, Hindi, Kazakh, Russian, Tamil, Ukrainian, Urdu; not Uzbek/Azerbaijani/Georgian/Armenian/Albanian/Macedonian/Bosnian/Nepali/Sinhala/Khmer/Lao/Mongolian/Filipino/Swahili/Amharic (those are keyboard-only, and Bosnian is not even a keyboard)
https://developer.apple.com/app-store/marketing/guidelines/ — App Store badge languages: has Ukrainian, Russian, Azerbaijani, Catalan, Hindi, Bangla, Urdu, Tamil and Tagalog; lacks the rest

https://partnermarketinghub.withgoogle.com/brands/google-play/google-play/lockups-icons-badges/ — official Google Play badge hub (play.google.com/badges redirects here); per-language list not visible without signing in
https://github.com/pioug/google-play-badges — third-party mirror of Google's localized badges, 76 codes; includes all asked-about languages except am
lproj folder names: standard Apple/ISO 639 codes from general knowledge; uz-Latn and bs not verified against an Apple page
